title: Bud Powell: Cootie Williams, Cafe Society and decline
summary: Hall's memories of Powell at the Savoy Ballroom with Cootie Williams, then his decline in Philadelphia.

bands.name: Billy Hicks and His Sizzling Six

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution

blocks.x: " What do you remember about Bud in those days?
Oh, Bud was terrific. I worked with Bud well, Bud, he merged with Cootie Williams orchestra, the big band at the Savoy Ballroom when I was still working there.
Along with Billy Hicks?
Yeah.
So you heard him then?
Yeah. And then he traveled with the Cootie Williams band, and of course, Bud lived a little too fast.

But in those days, I think, you know, in the middle fourties when he made those records, he was at the height of his, I mean, he also made great records after that but that was also one of his great periods.
He --
He was really in command of his powers and he was awesome when he got going.
Right, but then he worked at Cafe Society Downtown.
Oh, yeah?
Yeah.
With whom?
I forgot, but he was the pianist down there after the Cootie band, Cootie Williams' band. And then he started going down hill mentally.
But you said when you knew him in Cootie's band that he wasn't having those mental problems?
No. We had a pretty close rapport.
Well, it has been said by, you know, different observers and also maybe through things that Bud said, that one of his inspirations and models was Billy Kyle.
I wouldn't doubt that. We worked, when Illinois Jacquet left Lionel Hampton in the height of -- what was the name of it? that? "Flying Home."
"Flying Home."
"Flying Home," the very first band that he had and Bud was the pianist.
Really?
Yeah. In Philadelphia.
Yeah, that's right. Bud was from Willow Grove or --
Germantown.
Willow Grove.
Yeah, Willow Grove, Germantown. By this time I guess he was heavy on drugs, that damaged a lot and he couldn't pay off his bills.
